title: Design: Part Library entry page looks as in the design
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a Part Library entry, part A, stocked at the test location.
  • Make sure the app is in the Light theme.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1600 pixels wide with the page zoom at 100%, so the screen is as wide as the design boards.
  • Open the attached design picture of board 7.2 at 100% zoom, so you can compare the screen with it.
  • Start on the Part Library page.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A's entry is listed.

Step 2:

  • The browser tab reads "Library Part".
  • At the left a white card reads "Part details", then part A's name in bold with a blue pencil-on-lines (edit) icon to its right, then Part number, Category, Manufacturer, Measurement and Total parts.
  • To its right the title "Parts" heads a table with an arrow column, then Workplace, Bin location, Average cost, Sell price, Core charge, Remaining Quantity, Min and Max; the test location's row is listed.
  • The page shows the pencil as its only edit control and has no Delete button anywhere.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only), story SV-10825 (Story 12, Call the Shared Parts List the Part Library)

  • S11-R3: “Clicking a row opens that entry's detail page. The pencil beside the entry's name opens the "Edit Library Part" window, where the entry is edited and where its Delete button sits, bottom left. The detail page itself has no Delete button.”
  • S12-R12: “The browser tab titles read "Part Library" on the list and "Library Part" on an entry's detail page.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 20: “Yes, the board 7.2 note is out of date. Follow the page: the detail page has no Delete. Delete is in the "Edit Library Part" window (S11-R3).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "7.2 An entry opens its detail page". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above where the PRD speaks, and from the board pictures where it is silent about the look.

The board's note below says the entry can be deleted on this page. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 20) that the note is out of date: the page has no Delete button, as the PRD (S11-R3) says and the board's picture shows.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • library-02-p7-2-entry-detail.png

The design's own words:

  • “Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).”
